Featured in Development

  • Accelerating Performance by Incrementally Integrating Rust into Existing Codebase

    Lily Mara explains how to avoid high-risk software rewrites through incremental FFI refactoring. She shares how engineering teams can replace Python bottlenecks with Rust via PyO3, demonstrating how to achieve dramatic function-level speedups, seamless integration testing, and meaningful infrastructure cost savings without microservice overhead.

Featured in Architecture & Design

  • The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code

    Agentic LLM systems have moved from linear prompt chains to graph-based workflows and, more recently, code-executing harnesses. Chains are simple but fragile, graphs add branching, retries, and validation, and code harnesses verify outputs through execution. The article advises validating model outputs and choosing the least complex design that meets reliability, speed, and cost needs.

Featured in AI, ML & Data Engineering

  • Serving LLMs at Scale: The Hidden KV Cache Advantage

    Khawaja Shams shares a distributed systems perspective on scaling LLM inference stacks efficiently. He discusses practical strategies for optimizing GPU utilization, managing KV cache memory cliffs, leveraging tiered storage, reducing tail latency, and implementing disaggregated prefill and decode architectures to improve overall fleet performance, cost economics, and availability.

Featured in Culture & Methods

  • AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction

    Nathen Harvey shares insights from DORA research on AI adoption in software delivery. He explains why AI acts as an amplifier, how the DORA AI Capabilities Model drives outcomes, and why engineering leaders must evolve beyond bottlenecks like code reviews to achieve sustainable productivity, reduce delivery instability, and empower developers without burning out their teams.

Featured in DevOps

  • Wrangling Telemetry at Scale: A Guide to Self-Hosted Observability

    Colin Douch shares battle-tested strategies for building and scaling self-hosted observability stacks. He explains how to effectively correlate metrics, structured logs, and distributed traces using open-source tooling like Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, and Jaeger, while navigating the engineering trade-offs of avoiding SaaS vendor lock-in.

Summary

Mike Pirnat presents some tips and tricks, standard libraries and third party packages that make programming in Python a richer experience.

Bio

Mike Pirnat has 11 years of Python programming and over 15 years of web development, working at online greeting leader AG Interactive, where he serves as a wandering samurai, doer of deeds, righter of wrongs, integrator of systems, wrangler of code, bearer of standards, seeker of truth, advocate of excellence, educator, mentor, craftsman, and catalyst.
